description: Stacker - PlanBench-style block-stacking task. A single agent has a set of labeled blocks on a table; some may be stacked. The agent picks up, puts down, stacks, and unstacks blocks to reach a specified goal configuration. Reward is terminal (goal reached vs step-cap) plus intermediate signal on goal-distance delta. Fully observable, single-agent. Source instance set: PlanBench 2/4/6-step problems via maitrix-org/llm-reasoners.

state_space.trace_recommendation: Full ground-truth state per turn. State is small (block names + relations) so opponent-modeling vs in-character distinction does not apply here. Use the same ground_truth_state field across the trace for physis ingestion.

action_set.constraints: block must be on_table AND clear (nothing on top); hand must be empty
top must be in_hand; bottom must be clear (nothing on top); top != bottom
top must be clear AND on top of from; hand must be empty

intermediate_per_step.ground_truth: goal_distance_delta = goal_distance(prev) - goal_distance(current); positive when the agent moves blocks toward goal configuration, negative when it moves away
intermediate_per_step.shape: Dense - fires every action. goal_distance is number of (block,position) tuples in goal not yet matched by current state.

self_eval.format: free-form text per turn capturing agent's expectation of own move quality

terminal_condition.trigger: all goal predicates satisfied OR step budget exhausted

per_line_schema.reward: float - intermediate reward delta this step
per_line_schema.events: list of human-readable engine events (e.g., 'block A picked up', 'goal predicate on(B,C) now satisfied')

first_line_meta.match_id: str (run_id, distinct from instance_id since the same instance can be replayed)
first_line_meta.instance: {blocks, initial_stacks, initial_on_table, goal_stacks, goal_on_table, optimal_steps, difficulty}

last_line_meta.optimal_ratio: float (steps_taken / optimal_steps); null if optimal_steps is null/zero (instance unsolved or unknown optimum)

prior_art_anchors.name: PlanBench (Valmeekam, Kambhampati 2022-23)
prior_art_anchors.relevance: canonical Blockworld evaluation suite; LLM-direct accuracy is low at 4+ steps without scaffolding. Establishes that this is a genuine planning task, not pattern-matching.

prior_art_anchors.name: RAP (Hao et al. 2023)
prior_art_anchors.relevance: LLM as both world-model and MCTS searcher; strong Blockworld results. Demonstrates the in-context simulator pattern works for this task.
prior_art_anchors.import_target: world-model rollout pattern - have physis simulate next-state given (state, action) before committing to a move

prior_art_anchors.name: Algorithm Distillation (Laskin et al. 2022)
prior_art_anchors.relevance: in-context RL via trajectory-conditioned generation; the rationale for why our (s,a,r) trace accumulation should improve policy without weight updates.
prior_art_anchors.import_target: trace ordering convention - put most-similar past trajectories first in physis context to maximize transfer

prior_art_anchors.name: Voyager (Wang et al. 2023)
prior_art_anchors.relevance: iterative-prompting + self-verifier pattern. Even simple Blockworld benefits from a 'propose -> verify constraints -> commit or revise' inner loop.
prior_art_anchors.import_target: physis on-step inner loop - simulate proposed action against current state predicates, only emit action if simulation respects constraints

prior_art_anchors.name: LLM-Modulo (Kambhampati 2024)
prior_art_anchors.relevance: LLM as plan critic, not plan generator; pair LLM with external verifier. Stacker has cheap deterministic verification (block predicates) so LLM-Modulo's pattern is directly applicable.
prior_art_anchors.import_target: physis emits action; engine verifies; engine returns delta + violations (if any). Failed actions become explicit reflection content.

notes: Per JJ + Ray + Cody coordination 2026-04-26: Stacker is the Ludex-side Co-MVP for D-067 physis, paired with Echo x Avalon on LxM.
Source instance set: maitrix-org/llm-reasoners ships PlanBench Blockworld instances. Will adopt their (S,A,R) schema directly for first MVP run; reformat into trace structure on import.

Naming: this is 'Stacker' on the Ludex side to avoid collision with LxM's voxel-sandbox 'Blockworld' (per Cody's 2026-04-26 collision flag). The underlying task is the classic PlanBench block-stacking benchmark.

trace_export=committed because Stacker traces are very small (a typical 2-step instance trace ~5-15 KB; 6-step ~25-50 KB). At 100+ instances we still stay under 5 MB total, well below LxM Avalon's projected size. No early gitignore concern.

Single-agent and fully-observable, intentionally - opposite extremes to LxM Avalon (multi-agent, partial-obs). Together they bracket the design space for physis: Stacker tests pure planning learning; Avalon tests opponent modeling + belief reasoning. Cross-field abstractions in _meta.md should benefit from this contrast.
